subject: Trying to replicate a published MPlus analysis in Lavaan

messages.author: 5e6a37055298a087
messages.subject: Trying to replicate a published MPlus analysis in Lavaan
parts:
My first post here.  Apologies in advance, advice about good introductory texts may be needed, I'll come back to that.

I'm trying to replicate analyses in Nelson, T. D., B. S. Aylward, and J. R. Rausch. 2011. ‘Dynamic P-Technique for Modeling Patterns of Data: Applications to Pediatric Psychology Research’. Journal of Pediatric Psychology 36 (9): 959–68. doi:10.1093/jpepsy/jsr023 which has supplementary material with the following MPlus syntax:

TITLE:            Dynamic P-Technique Example for JPP

DATA:            FILE IS C:\PTechExampNegMood.dat;

VARIABLE:  NAMES ARE Pain PainLag Mood1 Mood1Lag

Mood2 Mood2Lag Mood3 Mood3Lag Mood4 Mood4Lag

Mood5 Mood5Lag;

MODEL:         Mood BY Mood1 (1);

        Mood BY Mood2 (2);

        Mood BY Mood3 (3);

        Mood BY Mood4 (4);

        Mood BY Mood5 (5);

 

        MoodLag BY Mood1Lag (1);

        MoodLag BY Mood2Lag (2);

        MoodLag BY Mood3Lag (3);

        MoodLag BY Mood4Lag (4);

        MoodLag BY Mood5Lag (5);

       

        Pain ON PainLag MoodLag;

        Mood ON PainLag MoodLag;

OUTPUT: Standardized;


And runs with the data (dat.csv attached) that is also in the supplementary material to the paper.  The Lavaan code I've used is:


require(lavaan)

dat <- read.csv(dat.csv)

colnames(dat) <- c("Pain",
                   "PainLag",
                   "Mood1",
                   "Mood1Lag",
                   "Mood2",
                   "Mood2Lag",
                   "Mood3",
                   "Mood3Lag",
                   "Mood4",
                   "Mood4Lag",
                   "Mood5",
                   "Mood5Lag")

model3 <- 'mood1 =~ Mood1
                  + Mood2
                  + Mood3
                  + Mood4
                  + Mood5
              moodLag =~ Mood1Lag
                     + Mood2Lag
                     + Mood3Lag
                     + Mood4Lag
                     + Mood5Lag
              mood1 ~ moodLag + PainLag
              Pain ~ moodLag + PainLag
              PainLag ~~ moodLag
              Pain ~~ mood1'
finalFit3 <- cfa(model3,data=dat)
summary(finalFit3,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)


The output shown in the paper, which clearly simplifies that MPlus model is:


What I'm getting from Lavaan is:

lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  32 iterations
## 
##   Number of observations                           199
## 
##   Estimator                                         ML
##   Minimum Function Test Statistic               52.688
##   Degrees of freedom                                50
##   P-value (Chi-square)                           0.371

and this:

Regressions:
##                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
##   mood1 ~                                                               
##     moodLag           0.435    0.086    5.042    0.000    0.427    0.427
##     PainLag           0.078    0.022    3.482    0.000    0.112    0.251
##   Pain ~                                                                
##     moodLag           0.867    0.227    3.826    0.000    0.594    0.264
##     PainLag           0.437    0.061    7.104    0.000    0.437    0.436
## 
## Covariances:
##                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
##   moodLag ~~                                                            
##     PainLag           0.344    0.123    2.783    0.005    0.502    0.223
##  .mood1 ~~                                                              
##    .Pain             -0.089    0.091   -0.979    0.327   -0.152   -0.081

Two things strike me as very odd here:
1) the df in paper from MPlus are said to by 54 and mine from Lavaan says 50.  I find myself 
counting things off and getting to 50 not 54 but I know that I haven't dealt with models with 
two latents and two observed predictors with no measurement model attached to them so I wonder
if I'm miscounting that and misspecifying the Lavaan.
2) the "diagonal" regressions from PainLag to mood1 and from moodLag to Pain in my output seem
to be reversed compared with those in that figure from the published paper.

Can anyone see things here that will help me?!

Now it's a very long time since I last used SEM software regularly (15+ years) and then 
it was just CFA with the then versions of LISREL and AMOS so I know I need to do some 
serious (re)learning.  I love R and have used it for pretty much all my stats work in the last 12+ years
and I like the look of Lavaan.  I've had a look at OpenMx and SEM but for the moment haven't worked
out how to specify this model in them.  I have access to modern AMOS and I can specify the 
mood measurement models in its visual model creator but it's refusing to let me put in the structural
regressions and covariances.


I'm currently working in a university with no maths or stats departments and I'm probably one of the

most, if not the most, statistically experienced person in my department.


If anyone can recommend contemporary introductory reading for these sorts of SEM models, particularly

ones focused on Lavaan (or the other R SEM systems), I'd be interested to hear that general advice as

well as any specific input on the above.


TIA,


Chris

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Trying to replicate a published MPlus analysis in Lavaan
parts:
The first thing that you are missing is the labels from the original Mplus syntax. The "(1)" through "(5)" in the Mplus syntax are labels, and when the same labels are used again, this imposes equality constraints on the parameters so labeled. These equality constraints are missing from your lavaan code.
     In lavaan syntax, you label parameters this way:
mood1 =~ a*Mood1 + b*Mood2 + ...
[[I think it is bad practice to have different variables differentiated only by uppercase / lowercase on the first letter, but that's just me]]
Labels must be alphabetical in lavaan--the numeric labels from the ecxample would be taken as fixed values assigned to the parameters. But a - e will work as well as 1 - 5.
     Imposing these 5 equality constraints, by using the same labels for the Mood and Moodlag indicators, will save you 4 DF. (The first indicator for Mood and for Moodlag will have its loading fixed to 1 by default, anyway, so they are already "equal," even without these constraints.)
     If you want a text on using lavaan, Alex Beaujean has one:

https://www.amazon.com/Latent-Variable-Modeling-Using-Step/dp/1848726996/ref=sr_1_fkmr0_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1504016041&sr=8-1-fkmr0&keywords=beaujean+lavaan
